scenes.title: 1947 Winnenden Clinic: Patient S. Reading Fine Print Sharp Yet Failing to Know a Tabletop Mirror & Family Portraits Until a Voice Speaks

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1947 European clinic consultation desk holding a fine-print eye-chart card (read 100% accurately), a brass-trimmed wooden tabletop mirror, three framed black-and-white family portrait photographs, and a doorway where a visiting family member mannequin steps in silently before speaking.

positions.who: Patient S. (mannequin in neat 1947 wool cardigan and collared shirt)
positions.where: reading tiny print cleanly, then gazing puzzled into the tabletop mirror and across three family portraits — before lighting up with instant recognition the second the visitor at the door speaks

positions.who: Joachim Bodamer (mannequin in 1947 crisp white physician coat)
positions.where: presenting the fine-print card, object tray, and portrait photographs to isolate pure face-identity loss

positions.who: Mother / Visitor mannequin (in 1947 coat and hat)
positions.where: standing silently at first (unrecognized), then speaking warmly and triggering instant joyful recognition

props.name: fine-print reading card & everyday object tray vs family portraits
props.period_detail: proves sharp 20/20 visual acuity and object naming alongside zero face ID

props.name: wooden-framed tabletop mirror
props.period_detail: stages Patient S. (and later Oliver Sacks) looking into a mirror without recognizing his own face

actions.verb_sequence: reads fine print aloud effortlessly -> looks into the tabletop mirror and family portraits shaking head blankly -> Visitor speaks one warm greeting -> Patient S. turns and rises immediately in warm recognition
notes intact visual acuity + intact voice identity vs selective *Prosop-Agnosie*

reactions.reaction: relieved warmth upon hearing the unmistakable voice

scenes.wardrobe: 1947 European clinical white coat with tie; wool cardigan and pleated trousers; 1947 tailored coat.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key European hospital window daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: He can read the smallest line on an eye chart — yet stares straight at his own face in a mirror and his own mother in a doorway until she speaks.

key_visual.description: a 1947 neurology clinic desk with a fine-print eye card, family portraits, and a tabletop mirror where a seated patient looks blankly at faces until recognizing a speaking visitor

scenes.title: 1985 Covert Recognition: Palm Sweat Knows Mom When Words Don't
scenes.era: 1985, University of Iowa neurology lab (Tranel & Damasio)

layout.description: Bright clinical table with stranger vs family portrait cards and a dual-pen electrodermal chart.

positions.where: shaking head 'Stranger' on every photo while the electrodermal pen jumps high exclusively on family portraits

props.name: family-vs-stranger photo deck & palmar conductance graph
props.period_detail: proves unconscious autonomic recognition survives without conscious face ID

actions.verb_sequence: slides stranger photo (flat line) -> slides spouse photo (patient says 'Don't know her' while needle jumps high)

reactions.reaction: contrasts covert prosopagnosia against its mirror twin, Capgras delusion

scenes.recognition_hook: Consciously she swears she has never seen her husband's photo in her life — while her sweat glands leap in instant recognition.

scenes.title: 1 in 50 People: The Uniform & Haircut Context Trap

layout.description: Bright split comparison: recognizable colleague in signature red glasses at her usual desk vs unrecognizable in casual hoodie after a haircut.

positions.where: recognizing colleague instantly by desk context & voice, vs hesitating when non-facial cues change

props.name: signature glasses / voice cue card ('~2% Congenital Prevalence')
props.period_detail: destigmatizes why 1 in 50 adults rely on context and voice

actions.verb_sequence: says 'Hey Jordan, it's Maya!' -> instant warm smile and handshake

reactions.reaction: easy social connection once name + voice anchor identity

scenes.recognition_hook: Roughly one in fifty people around you navigates faces by hairstyle, stride, and voice — one friendly name check bridges the gap instantly.

scenes.title: Oliver Sacks & The Friendly Mirror Apology

layout.description: Warm sunlit bookshop doorway with a tall bevel-edged wall mirror.

positions.where: stepping aside politely tipping his hat to 'another bearded gentleman' in the mirror, then chuckling warmly upon realizing it is his own reflection

props.name: full-length bevelled bookshop mirror & notebook
props.period_detail: humanizes congenital prosopagnosia with humor and grace

actions.verb_sequence: tips hat to mirror -> realizes reflection matches his own move -> laughs and jots a note

scenes.recognition_hook: Even world-famous neurologist Oliver Sacks once apologized for bumping into a bearded stranger — who turned out to be himself in a mirror.
